biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E / V600K
biomarkers.clinical_use: BRAF + MEK inhibitor combinations: dabrafenib+trametinib, encorafenib+binimetinib, vemurafenib+cobimetinib. Adjuvant dabrafenib+trametinib (COMBI-AD). BRAF-targeted therapy vs IO first-line — DREAMseq supports IO first in many patients

biomarkers.name: NRAS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common driver mutation with prognostic/biologic relevance, but no standard approved direct targeted therapy in melanoma; binimetinib (MEK inhibitor) showed modest benefit in NRAS-mutant disease (NEMO trial)

biomarkers.name: KIT
biomarkers.clinical_use: Imatinib, nilotinib in KIT-mutant melanoma (especially exon 11, 13); higher in acral/mucosal

biomarkers.name: NF1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Major genomic subtype in cutaneous melanoma; no established standard targeted therapy, but biologically relevant MAPK-pathway driver

biomarkers.name: PD-L1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Not required for IO use; combination nivolumab+ipilimumab or nivolumab+relatlimab (LAG-3) may be used regardless of PD-L1

biomarkers.name: LAG-3
biomarkers.clinical_use: Nivolumab + relatlimab (anti-LAG-3) approved first-line advanced melanoma (RELATIVITY-047), but tumor LAG-3 IHC is not required as a companion diagnostic

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.prevalence: Very high (UV-signature; among highest across tumours)

biomarkers.name: LDH
biomarkers.clinical_use: AJCC 8 distant metastatic subcategorization incorporates CNS disease (M1d) and LDH; elevated LDH is strongly prognostic and used for monitoring

biomarkers.name: S100B
biomarkers.clinical_use: European practice for monitoring; less used in US

biomarkers.name: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)
biomarkers.clinical_use: BRAF, NRAS tracking; MRD detection; emerging role

biomarkers.name: Ulceration + Breslow thickness + mitotic rate
biomarkers.clinical_use: Ulceration is major upstaging factor (AJCC 8); Breslow drives staging and sentinel node decisions; mitotic rate is prognostic but no longer a primary AJCC 8 T-category criterion

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Atypical melanocytes at dermoepidermal junction with pagetoid upward spread and dermal invasion
variants: superficial spreading (~70%, radial then vertical growth)
nodular (rapid vertical growth, often minimal/absent radial growth phase)
lentigo maligna melanoma (chronically sun-damaged skin, older patients)
desmoplastic (spindle cells in dense collagen, neurotropic)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: AJCC staging by Breslow thickness and ulceration; mitotic rate is prognostic but not the primary AJCC 8 staging determinant

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Prototypically 'hot' — UV-driven high TMB, TIL infiltration prognostic, exceptional IO responsiveness across the disease
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Desmoplastic variant has extensive fibrous stroma; other variants have variable dermal reaction

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Cutaneous melanocytes at basal layer of epidermis and in hair follicles
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Neural crest — melanocytes migrate from neural crest to skin during embryogenesis
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Melanocytic differentiation (S100+, HMB-45+, Melan-A+, SOX10+, MITF+) with variable pigmentation; nevus → dysplastic nevus → melanoma progression can occur in a subset, but many melanomas arise de novo
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: MITF is master lineage transcription factor — MITF-high (differentiated), MITF-intermediate (proliferative), MITF-low (invasive/dedifferentiated) cell states interconvert; phenotype switching drives treatment resistance
